exemptions.reason: NEW-1 (owner-approved mockup 'Review empty state options', option C) replaced Review's three same-shaped empty-state buttons with a project-aware sheet index. Its primary control is the full-width tappable PROJECT CARD (name over drawing count, thumb-height, bordered, RADIUS.md) — a genuinely new, deliberate shape the owner asked for by name, distinct from the screen's one text link ('Upload a file without a project'/'Upload file'), which is a borderless link-style button, not a card. The old buttons' single shared signature no longer exists on this surface, so the surface's own budget of 1 now covers the text link and the card is the one added shape. Both use only design tokens (RADIUS, FONT_SIZE, CONTROL_H.touch, SPACE); a code fix cannot remove this signature without dropping the card the owner's design calls for, or restyling the link as a card, which would be the wrong reason to change either.

Owner report — the Dashboard Locations map card's 'N projects' location(s) need fixing' link used to land on the Site Planner's plain, unfiltered project list with nothing marking which projects it meant. The Sites panel row now carries a small 'no location' flag next to any site with no origin (src/workspaces/site-planner/MapFinder.jsx's `rowFlagBadgeStyle`), the same standing-fact badge shape the existing 'no boundary' flag already uses on this same row (identical radius/height/padding/fontSize AND color — one shared style object, not a bespoke variant) — but that sibling flag's own precondition (a site with a boundary field but no drawn boundary) is never true in this crawl's fixture, so it has never itself been measured as a signature on this surface, and this is the first member of that shared shape this particular crawl has ever counted here. A code fix cannot remove this signature without either dropping the flag the owner's report asked for, or resizing it to coincidentally match an unrelated control already on the surface, which would be the wrong reason to change either one.

The global help/report control (src/app/HelpReportControl.jsx) is a persistent, fixed bottom-right FAB the app shell mounts once, on every route — the owner's own request, so the control being everywhere is the point, not drift. It renders one uniform signature (radius:8px/RADIUS.md since B1176976, padding:0px, fontSize:12px) on every whole-page surface this crawl visits — height is 30px (CONTROL_H.lg) under this crawl's fine-pointer, no-touch context since B1162016, 44px only under a coarse/touch pointer, never both at once; the surfaces that scope to a sub-region only (App header, the Main menu popovers, Tool rail) don't see it because it lives outside that DOM subtree, which is why only the whole-page surfaces above needed a budget lift. A single shared implementation, one exemption line per affected surface, never a per-surface variant.

Leaflet's own bundled zoom stack (+/− at its vendor font-size), "Find my location" locate button, and the scale bar are third-party chrome — docs/DESIGN.md's radius section (Documented exceptions #4) already carries the zoom-stack/locate-button radius override and the scale-bar non-exception as the accepted boundary of what this token scale reaches. Their child <a>/<div> nodes are deliberately radius:0 BY THE APP'S OWN CSS (the rounded corner the user sees comes from the parent .leaflet-bar container's overflow:hidden clip, not the button), so a per-button override here would fight the exact mechanism that already unified their visible shape with the app's own RADIUS.md. The one thing left off-scale (the zoom glyphs' 22px font) is Leaflet's own vendor CSS (.leaflet-touch .leaflet-control-zoom-in/-out), not an app literal.

NEW-1 (owner chat block, 2026-09-05) split the old Yield panel's flood/detention/mitigation work into its own Drainage tab and left Yield's Land Use table with a single 'Drainage →' ActionLink in its place — a genuinely new, permanent, deliberate control, not incidental drift. It is the shared ActionLink component (src/workspaces/site-planner/components/ActionLink.jsx) at its own default style, so it is not a bespoke shape; every other ActionLink usage already inside the Yield panel (Set unit prices, Set $/CY, Set $/SY or LF) only renders once its own conditional/disclosure state is reached, which this crawl's default-view pass never opens, so this is the first ActionLink this particular crawl has ever measured inside this surface at all — not a second, competing shape alongside an existing one. A code fix cannot remove this signature without either removing the link the owner's own architecture calls for, or duplicating an already-rendered control's exact style by coincidence, which would be the wrong reason to change either one.

AppHeader.jsx's wordmark/logo button (title "Dashboard: all projects") paints no border and no background (background:transparent, border:none) — it is a hit-target around the BrandMark, not a visible chip. Nothing renders for the eye to compare against another shape, so it is not the kind of drift this budget exists to bound. Giving it a real chip's chrome (a border/fill it has never had) to make its signature merge would ADD visible clutter around the logo — the opposite of the ask — so it stays a documented, permanent exception rather than a value change.

note: HARD BUDGET for ui-audit/ui-inventory.mjs's per-surface DISTINCT CONTROL SIGNATURE count (NEW-1, B1038016) — supersedes the old ratchet-only control-signature-ceiling.json (B982402), which only ever forbade a surface's count from GROWING past whatever it happened to measure the day it was written and so could never force a real reduction. A surface's raw signature count must be <= bySurface[surface] + the sum of every exemption's `count` that names that surface (see `effectiveCeiling` in ui-inventory.mjs) — exemptions ADD to the ceiling, they never subtract from the reported raw count, and every exemption is printed on every run, pass or fail. Regenerate a surface's OWN bySurface number only by hand, after a session genuinely lowers it through real control convergence (or, for a first-time surface, a first honest measurement) — never edit it to silence a real regression, and never add an exemption for a signature that a real code fix could remove instead. Every number here was set from a real post-fix measurement — see BACKLOG.md B1038016 for the per-surface reasoning and what was converged to reach it. CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (x2): "Map landing page (comp mode)" 15->16 and "Map landing page (selecting parcels)" 17->18. FIRST correction: the ORIGINAL 2026-09-01 numbers were measured from this repo's Claude Code sandbox, whose egress proxy allowlists only a few hosts and cannot reach Supabase or any of the real county/statewide ArcGIS hosts this crawl's landing view tries — so CompsPanel.jsx's "+ New comps"/"Import (KML)" buttons (gated `!loading && !loadError`, behind a real Supabase fetchAllComps() call) and MapFinder.jsx's selection-guidance tooltip (data-testid="select-parcels-tip", gated `!err`, cleared by a real county-GIS parcel-layer fetch succeeding) never rendered in the sandbox, while real CI (a GitHub Actions runner with normal network access) measured one more signature on each, deterministically (run 33581085858, job 100095330406, reproduced identically across three separate runs). SECOND correction (same day, same items): a raised budget number alone left the underlying crawl still environment-dependent, so docs/UI-INVENTORY.md (which embeds the raw counts as text) could never be regenerated byte-identically between this sandbox and CI — `--check`'s literal diff against the committed file would fail forever from here. Root-caused precisely (confirmed via curl: Supabase and every county GIS host this crawl reaches are blocked with a fast 403 from the sandbox's own proxy in well under a second, so no wait time could ever bridge it) and fixed at the source: `ui-inventory.mjs`'s `mockExternalNetwork` now intercepts every external request for these two surfaces and fulfills it with a generic, minimally-valid SUCCESSFUL response, so both surfaces settle to the identical rendered state (verified byte-for-byte against CI's own captured output) in every environment, deterministically. The counts above (16/18, effective ceiling 20/22) are therefore the real, permanently reproducible measurement, not a one-time CI snapshot. THIRD correction, 2026-09-03 (B850016/NEW-11): "Map landing page (comp mode)" 17->18, effective ceiling 21->22. B850016 fixed the owner-reported bug where the centre Site/Comp toggle and the left rail's Sites/Comps tab were coupled — the crawl's own `prep` step for this surface drives the state by clicking ONLY the centre toggle (`SiteCompSwitch`), which pre-fix ALSO flipped the left rail to the Comps tab (the coupling bug itself), so this surface's every prior baseline was measured with the COMPS panel's controls incidentally showing beneath the comp-mode toolbar. Post-fix that click legitimately leaves the rail on Sites (its own last, correct, decoupled state) — the SITES panel's own controls (the filter input, the sort select, a status-group header, its drag-reorder handle, a status dot) now show instead, one net signature more than the Comps panel's set did. This is the intended, owner-directed behavior change working correctly, not drift to silence — the crawl's `aria-label` selector was also updated in the same commit (the toggle's accessible name changed from "Browse sites or comps" to "What an address search creates" as part of the same fix, since it no longer browses anything).
